events.region: Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20
NM...

* Until 415 PM EDT.

* At 312 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over Mayport, or
31 nm north of Saint Augustine, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Atlantic Beach, Mayport, Talbot Island, Nassau Sound Approach Buoy
6a, Saint Johns Lighted Buoy, and Jacksonville Beach.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Brazoria, TX; Galveston, TX; Harris, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
counties, Brazoria, Galveston and Harris.

* WHEN...Until 415 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 211 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Very heavy rain rates are occurring which will
cause urban and small stream flooding. Overflowing poor
drainage areas will cause minor flooding in the advisory
area. Be especially careful on feeder roads where
construction is occurring. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Southwestern Pasadena, Pearland, League City, Friendswood,
Alvin, South Houston, Santa Fe, Webster, Manvel, Greater
Hobby Area, South Belt / Ellington, Clear Lake, Macgregor,
Greater Eastwood, Greater Third Ward, Astrodome Area, Second
Ward, Midtown Houston, Downtown Houston and University Place.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Frederick County in north central Maryland...
Northeastern Washington County in north central Maryland...

112 with apparent temperatures between 110 and 120 degrees. Major
Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In Arizona, Parker Valley and Yuma. In California,
Chuckwalla Valley, Imperial County West, Imperial Valley, Palo
Verde Valley, and Salton Sea.

exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
